dimensions.name: Task Success (outcome verifier, pass rate over trials)
dimensions.scoring_formula: pass_rate = trials whose verifier reward >= the entry's pass_threshold (default 1) / trials; score = round(100 * pass_rate) snapped to the nearest tier (env_runner.run_c6 -> run_benchmark._snap_to_tier). With 3 trials this is exact; with 5 trials, e.g. 4/5 = 80 snaps to 67

dimensions.name: Code quality (LLM judge: Readability, Maintainability, Robustness + 1-2 case-specific items)
dimensions.scoring_formula: mean over trials of quality_score = 100 x mean of item scores (perfect 1 / accept 0.6 / bad 0); items: 3 common in evaluation/rubrics/coding_quality.json + 1-2 per case in evaluation/rubrics/tasks/<ID>.json

score_synthesis.formula: No combined score: D1 (pass rate, hidden-test verifier, unchanged) and D2 (mean code-quality score, LLM judge) are reported side by side per entry and model. Trials flagged invalid by the validity audit (answer access / test tampering) are listed separately and should be re-run.
notes: Multiple trials are needed because single agent runs are high-variance; our runs use 3 trials (--trials 3; the CLI default is 5).
Infrastructure failures (sandbox start, build) are recorded per trial as infra_error and count as 0; rerun any trial that shows infra_error.
D1 has no LLM judge: every entry has an objective, verifier-defined outcome. D2 is graded by one LLM judge (Claude Opus 5.5).
C7 entries are representative of routine engineering work (bug fixes, feature additions, environment tasks). They are not chosen for discrimination; most strong models pass most of them.
Each entry keeps its pre-restructure ID in former_id (see results/id_mapping.json).

verifier_contract.runs_in: the task environment after the agent finishes; the agent never sees the verifier
verifier_contract.reward: binary 0/1, or continuous in [0,1] with a per-entry pass_threshold (DeepSWE-style entries)
